title_en: The Causality Weapon: When State Media Calls a U.S. Bear Market, the Bottom Is Near
excerpt_en: Nasdaq down 5%, Nvidia down 14%, Bitcoin under $60,000 — when does this cross-market rout end? Line up the last four times Chinese state media declared a U.S. bear market against what the S&P 500 did next, and the answer may already be written.
body_en:
The Nasdaq is down more than 5%, Nvidia dropped 14% in a day, Bitcoin has fallen below $60,000 and gold is closing in on $3,500. When does this cross-market rout end?

Probably soon — because the causality weapon has already been fired. On November 21, Xinhua published a roundup headlined "Tech-stock plunge drags U.S. stocks into correction territory." Judging by the track record, whenever Chinese state media start reporting a U.S. bear market in earnest, the bottom is usually not far away. If they go on to declare that "U.S. stocks have officially entered a technical bear market," that will basically prove the bottom is in.

This is not superstition; it is a matter of record. Line up the last four times state media reported a U.S. bear market against what the S&P 500 did next:

Christmas Eve 2018: bottom one day after the report

On December 24, 2018, U.S. stocks plunged: the Dow fell 2.91%, the S&P 500 fell 2.71%, the Nasdaq fell 2.21% and slipped into bear-market territory. On December 25, CCTV ran a long report — "A 6-trillion-yuan crash! U.S. stocks suffer their worst Christmas Eve in history!" — citing Bank of America Merrill Lynch analysts who said the sell-off could last at least six months.

What happened? When the report aired, U.S. markets were closed for Christmas. On the next trading day, December 26, the S&P 500 surged about 5% and gradually recovered from there. "At least six months" turned out to be one more day of falling.

March 2020: bottom eleven days after the report

On March 12, 2020, China News Service published "U.S. stocks plunge again! Dow enters a technical bear market — why is there still no bottom?", writing that "the 11-year bull market in U.S. stocks may be coming to an end."

The close behind that report, on March 11, was 2,741.38. The index fell another 18.4% or so and bottomed at 2,237.40 on March 23 — eleven days after the report. By year-end, the S&P 500 had rebounded to 3,756.07.

2022: the one exception — a four-month wait

On June 14, 2022, CCTV News ran "U.S. stocks fall sharply, S&P 500 enters a bear market." This was state media's proudest call: the close behind it, on June 13, was 3,749.63, and although the market first rebounded hard, it did not bottom until October 12 at 3,577.03 — a full four months after the report, another 4.6% lower.

The only exception in four cases. And even then, after the report there was only one final leg down left.

April 2025: the fastest slap in the face

On April 7, 2025, CCTV's website reported that U.S. stocks had shed $5.4 trillion over the previous two trading days and that the Nasdaq had fallen into a technical bear market. The April 4 close was 5,074.08; the index bottomed at 4,982.77 on April 8 and surged about 9.5% in a single day on April 9.

From report to rebound: one day.

Crashes and rallies get two different pens

Someone might object that state media do report rallies too. They do. But put the headlines side by side and the two are written with entirely different pens.

A crash is the sky falling; a rally is a dying flash of light. The same pen writes two different kinds of news.

This time: wait and see

The scoreboard:

YearState-media bear-market reportTime to the bottom

2026Xinhua, Nov 21To be observed

The 2018, 2020 and 2025 reports all landed almost exactly on the bottom; 2022 is the only exception.

Perhaps they have learned their lesson this time: CCTV has not rushed to say "U.S. stocks have entered a technical bear market" — even though the Nasdaq is only a step away from one — and Xinhua's roundup went no further than "correction territory."

So let us wait and see.

Nothing here is investment advice.

Postscript (Nov 24): A few hours after this article went live, U.S. markets closed on Monday, and 'to be observed' got its first data point: Nvidia jumped 31.5% to $165.05, its biggest single-day gain since 2003; the Nasdaq-100 rose 6.86% and the S&P 500 rose 4.73%, both their best day since April 2025. Jensen Huang's return was the trigger, but mind the timeline: Xinhua's roundup came out on November 21, and the frenzy hit on the first full trading day after it. The causality weapon's 2026 record opens with this entry: first trading day after the report — a surge. Granted, it is only day one; in 2022 the wait was four months. The observation continues.
